  "content": "# SRS: issue_39 (v1)
## 1. Purpose and scope
- S-01: "Searches sometimes return data that doesn't match what's in the db??"

- S-03: "Example: I search for something, tweak the returned dicts a bit for display purposes (like formatting a field), and later when I run the SAME search again the old tweaked values show up even though I never called update or anything."
- S-04: "It's like tinydb remembers my display edits."
- S-05: "If I restart the script the data is fine again, so the file itself is OK."
- S-06: "It only happens within one run and only sometimes (maybe only when I edit the dicts I got back?)."
- S-07: "Is this a caching bug? Can you make it so the documents you get back from search/all are just... normal dicts you can safely edit without side effects?"

## 2. Actors
| ID | Actor | Basis | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| ACT-1 | Developer / User | STATED | S-03, S-07 |

## 3. Constraints
| ID | Statement | Basis | Source | Gate |
|---|---|---|---|---|

## 4. Functional requirements
| ID | Statement | Basis | Source | Priority | Gate | AC |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| FR-001 | The search and retrieval methods shall return deep copies (or independent copies) of documents such that modifying the returned dictionary objects does not mutate internal database cache or stored table documents. | STATED | S-03, S-07 | UNSET | CLARIFY | AC-001-1 |

## 5. Non-functional reqs
| ID | Statement | Basis | Source | Priority | Gate | AC |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

## 6. Acceptance criteria
| AC-id | Requirement | Criterion (given/when/then or measurable) |
|---|---|---|>
| AC-001-1 | FR-001 | Given a table containing a document, When a search or retrieval (e.g. search, all) is executed and the returned dictionary is modified in place, Then subsequent searches or retrievals return the original unmodified document values without side effects from the previous edits. |
| AC-NFR1-1 | NFR-001 | Given retrieval benchmarks, When returning copies of documents, Then the execution time overhead per document shall not exceed TBD milliseconds. |

## 7. Dependencies and risks

  "content": "# Spec: Prevent Search Result Mutation Side Effects in TinyDB
## Source
- GitHub Issue #39: "Searches sometimes return data that doesn't match what's in the db??"
- Key sentences: "Example: I search for something, tweak the returned dicts a bit for display purposes (like formatting a field), and later when I run the SAME search again the old tweaked values show up even though I never called update or anything.", "Can you make it so the documents you get back from search/all are just... normal dicts you can safely edit without side effects?"

## Requirements
- FR-001: The search and retrieval methods shall return deep copies (or independent copies) of documents such that modifying the returned dictionary objects does not mutate internal database cache or stored table documents.
- NFR-001: Document retrieval shall not introduce unacceptable latency regressions [TBD] when returning copies.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a table containing a document, When a search or retrieval (e.g. search, all) is executed and the returned dictionary is modified in place, Then subsequent searches or retrievals return the original unmodified document values without side effects from the previous edits.
- Given retrieval benchmarks, When returning copies of documents, Then the execution time overhead per document shall not exceed TBD milliseconds.

## Assumptions and open questions
- Question Q-01: What is the exact acceptable performance overhead limit for returning deep copies of query results? Default chosen: TBD, because no latency threshold was specified in the issue.
- Assumption ASM-01: Deep-copying documents on search/retrieval will prevent reference aliasing without breaking existing non-mutating consumers.
"
